name: calendar
title: Calendar
tagline: A one-month calendar grid whose day-count (leap rule) and the weekday of the 1st (derived) lay out the dates; mark dates and step this/next/last with wrap.
description: One month laid out as a seven-column day-of-week grid: the dates 1 to the end of the month in week rows, with the right number of leading blanks before the 1st. The author writes the month and year and everything is derived — the number of days (28 or 29 for February by the leap-year rule) and the weekday the 1st falls on (Zeller's congruence), so the grid is computed from the date and cannot be laid out wrong; an abstract month (a chosen number of days starting on a chosen weekday) is available when no real year is wanted. Dates can be labelled, highlighted or hidden as "?" for a question. A relation steps one date on — the next or previous day, the same day next or previous week, or a number of days — and the target and whether it stays in the month or wraps into the next or previous month are derived, drawn as a connector to the target cell or annotated when it spills over. A warm stem sentence restates the figure in words. (The periodic ring of months / days / seasons is the separate time/cycle-wheel model.)
whenToUse: Reach for this to read a calendar month and reason across its dates: find a date, work out which day of the week a date falls on, the same day next week (+7), the day after the last day of the month, and leap years. Give month + year for a real month (the day-count and the weekday of the 1st are derived — author nothing about the layout); give days + startDay for an abstract teaching month with no particular year. Common configurations: read a month — month + year with marks on the dates that matter (label / highlight); which date? — a mark with occlude true ("the trip is the last Friday — which date?"); this/next/last — a relation from a date (nextDay / prevDay / nextWeek / prevWeek, or by ± a number of days), relation.occlude to ask for the answer; the relation draws a connector to the target when it stays in the month, or annotates the date in the next/previous month when it wraps. weekStart defaults to monday (the UK convention); set sunday for a Sunday-first calendar. Keep the same month + weekStart across a lesson. Staged builds suit it: open on the plain month and reveal a relation's answer, accumulate the marked events one per stage, or work a month-end wrap. For naming the months / days / seasons as a repeating cycle, or "3 months after November", use the time/cycle-wheel model instead. Synonyms teachers use: calendar, month, date, day of the week, weekday, the 14th, next week, leap year, days in a month.

month.description: The month, as a name ("June") or number (1–12). With year, the number of days and the weekday of the 1st are both derived — a real calendar month. Default 1 (January).

year.description: The four-digit year. Enables the real calendar: the number of days (28/29 for February by the leap-year rule) and the weekday the 1st falls on are computed from month + year. Omit only for an abstract month (then give days / startDay).

days.description: Override the number of days in the month (28–31), for an abstract month when no year is given. Ignored when month + year already derive the day count.

startDay.description: Override the weekday the 1st falls on — a day name ("Thursday") or 0–6 counting from the configured week start. For an abstract month; ignored when month + year derive it.

weekStart.description: Which day heads the week columns. Default "monday" (the UK convention).

marks.description: Dates to label, highlight or occlude.

day.description: The date (1–31). A date past the end of the month is ignored.

label.description: A short caption under the date (e.g. "Trip"). Keep it brief — it sits inside the cell. Optional.

occlude.description: Hide the date number as "?" — "which day is the trip on?". Default false.

relation.description: Step one date on to another and show the link — this/next/last on the calendar. The target date and whether it stays in-month or wraps into the next / previous month are derived.

op.description: The step: nextDay (+1), prevDay (−1), nextWeek (+7, the same weekday next week), prevWeek (−7). Use by instead for another number of days.

by.description: Signed number of days to step, as an alternative to op (e.g. 7, −1, 10). Overrides op if both are given.

occlude.description: Hide the target date — "what is the date a week later?". Default false.

label.description: Override the derived readout text. Omit for the computed one.

weekdayHeader.description: Show the day-of-week column headings (Mon, Tue …). Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional terse line below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Distinct from stem. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

stem.description: Optional stem sentence in a warm band below the figure — the verbal twin of the model, in a child's reading voice. Use "?" where the figure occludes the answer so the sentence never leaks it.
